article.title: Elderly Palestinian woman killed, 19 wounded by Israeli violence in West Bank
article.author: Aseel Saleh
article.content: Monday, November 16, marked another horrific night for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank after illegal Israeli settlers launched simultaneous assaults against civilians in the eastern governorate of Jericho, and the southern governorate of Bethlehem. Israeli settlers opened fire on Palestinian residents in Ad-Duyuk at-Tahta village west of Jericho, killing 72-year-old woman Fadda Fheidat and injuring 10 others. A relative of Fheidat told Palestine News and Information Agency WAFA , that the Israeli forces prohibited the family from holding a funeral procession in the village on Tuesday, November 17. Israeli soldiers also beat a Palestinian photographer working for the same news agency on Tuesday morning while he was covering the events in the village. The photographer sustained fractures and bruises and was transferred to a hospital to receive medical treatment. The deadly assault on Ad-Duyuk at-Tahta came two weeks after Israeli settlers – backed by the right-wing settlement organization Nachala – seized several Palestinian homes in the village, displacing dozens of residents. Meanwhile, eight Palestinians were injured in the town of Tuqu’, south of Bethlehem, late Monday after an Israeli settler rammed them with his vehicle. According to a recent report released by the United Nations, over 1,122 Palestinians, including 246 children, were killed in attacks carried out by Israeli forces and illegal colonists in the occupied West Bank between October 7, 2023, and July 24, 2026.
